  3527	\begin{lemma}[The finite terminal-chain Wick formula]\label{L:terminal-wick}

  3529	  $d = 1,2,3$, with covariance $\mathcal{K}(s,y;r,z)$. Suppose that $V =
  3530	  \sup_{s,y}\E|\mathcal{W}(s,y)|^2 < \infty$, and that the field is jointly
  3531	  continuous in mean square on each open cell of a finite partition of $[0,T]$,
  3532	  times $\R^d$. Define $Y_0 = 1$ and
  3533	  \[
  3534	    Y_n(T,x)=\int\prod_{j=1}^n\mathcal{W}(s_j,y_j)
  3535	    \,\mathsf{g}_n^{T,x}(\ud\boldsymbol s,\ud\boldsymbol y).
  3536	  \]

  3538	  \begin{equation}\label{E:terminal-term-majorant}
  3539	    \|Y_n(T,x)\|_2
  3540	    \le\sqrt{(2n-1)!!}\,V^{n/2}\frac{T^{2n}}{(2n)!},
  3541	    \qquad n\ge1.
  3542	  \end{equation}

  3544	  (s_1,\ldots,s_m,r_1,\ldots,r_n)$ and $\boldsymbol\eta =
  3545	  (y_1,\ldots,y_m,z_1,\ldots,z_n)$. Then

  3547	    \E[Y_m(T,x)Y_n(T,x)]
  3548	    =\sum_{D\in\Pi_k}\mathcal{T}_{m,n,D}^{\mathcal{K}}(T,x),

  3553	      \mathcal{T}_{m,n,D}^{\mathcal{K}}

  3556	      \int_{(\R^d)^m\times(\R^d)^n}\\

  3630	\begin{lemma}[Uniform series tails from scaled moments]\label{L:uniform-series-tail}
  3631	  Fix $(T,x)$. For each positive regularization pair $(\epsilon,\delta)$, let
  3632	  $Y_n^{\epsilon,\delta}$ be the terms of Lemma~\ref{L:terminal-wick} for a
  3633	  field with nonnegative covariance. Write $u^{\epsilon,\delta}(r) =
  3634	  \sum_{n\ge0}r^nY_n^{\epsilon,\delta}$. Suppose that, for some $r > 1$ and
  3635	  finite $B_r$,
  3636	  \[
  3637	    \sup_{\epsilon,\delta>0}
  3638	    \E|u^{\epsilon,\delta}(r)|^2\le B_r,
  3639	    \qquad
  3640	    Y_n^{\epsilon,\delta}\longrightarrow X_n
  3641	    \text{ in }L^2\text{ for each fixed }n.
  3642	  \]
  3643	  Then $u = \sum_{n\ge0}X_n$ converges absolutely in $L^2$,
  3644	  $u^{\epsilon,\delta}(1) \to u$ in $L^2$, and
  3645	  \begin{equation}\label{E:uniform-series-tail}
  3646	    \|Y_n^{\epsilon,\delta}\|_2,\ \|X_n\|_2
  3647	    \le B_r^{1/2}r^{-n},\qquad
  3648	    \left\|\sum_{n>N}Y_n^{\epsilon,\delta}\right\|_2,
  3649	    \left\|\sum_{n>N}X_n\right\|_2
  3650	    \le\frac{B_r^{1/2}r^{-(N+1)}}{1-r^{-1}}.
  3651	  \end{equation}
  3652	  If also $\E|u^{\epsilon,\delta}(1)|^2 \le B_1$ uniformly, then $\E|u|^2 \le
  3653	  B_1$.
  3654	\end{lemma}
  3655	
  3656	\begin{proof}
  3657	  Lemma~\ref{L:terminal-wick} gives absolute $L^2$ convergence of every
  3658	  regularized series and nonnegative mixed moments. Its scaled second moment
  3659	  therefore contains the nonnegative term $r^{2n}\E|Y_n^{\epsilon,\delta}|^2$,
  3660	  so $r^{2n}\E|Y_n^{\epsilon,\delta}|^2 \le B_r$. Taking the fixed-order $L^2$
  3661	  limit proves the same bound for $X_n$. The geometric series and the triangle
  3662	  inequality give all estimates in~\eqref{E:uniform-series-tail}, including
  3663	  absolute convergence.
  3664	
  3665	  For each $N$, write both full series as their first $N+1$ terms and their
  3666	  tails. Their distance is at most
  3667	  \[
  3668	    \frac{2B_r^{1/2}r^{-(N+1)}}{1-r^{-1}}
  3669	    +\left\|\sum_{n=0}^N(Y_n^{\epsilon,\delta}-X_n)\right\|_2.
  3670	  \]

  3672	  \infty$. This proves convergence of the full regularized solution; it was not
  3673	  assumed. Continuity of the $L^2$ norm passes the bound $B_1$ to $u$. This
  3674	  proves Lemma~\ref{L:uniform-series-tail}.
  3675	\end{proof}

  4801	## UniformSeriesTail (whole result)
  4802	
  4803	Formalizes `L:uniform-series-tail` (`notes/notes_stratonovich_ham_second_moment.tex`
  4804	at `975feb3`; statement lines 3630-3654 with the display
  4805	`E:uniform-series-tail`, lines 3645-3651; proof lines 3656-3675), with every
  4806	conclusion proved and one supplied input from `L:terminal-wick` (lines
  4807	3527-3572), the structure `TerminalWickInput`. The TeX proof cites exactly two
  4808	facts from `L:terminal-wick` (lines 3657-3658): absolute `L^2` convergence of
  4809	every regularized series and nonnegative mixed moments. `TerminalWickInput mu Y r`
  4810	states these two facts for one family `Y : N -> L^2` and the given `r`:
  4811	`sum_n ||r^n Y_n||_2 < infinity` (`L:terminal-wick` gives it for every real or
  4812	complex `r`, lines 3570-3571) and `E[Y_m Y_n] >= 0` for all `m, n` (its Wick
  4813	formula with nonnegative pairing integrals when the covariance is nonnegative,
  4814	and zero when `m + n` is odd, lines 3566-3568). Nothing else about the Gaussian
  4815	field, the chain measures `g_n^{T,x}` or the Wick formula is used, so the Lean
  4816	statements hold for an arbitrary family of real `L^2(Omega)` elements with these
  4817	two facts; the identification of `Y_n^{eps,delta}` with the terms of
  4818	`L:terminal-wick` for a field with nonnegative covariance is not formalized. The
  4819	fixed point `(T,x)` is implicit in the family. `L^2(Omega)` is Mathlib's
  4820	`Lp R 2 mu` (real-valued), `E|f|^2` is written as the Bochner integral of
  4821	`f(omega)^2` (equal to `||f||^2` by `integral_sq_eq_norm_sq`, a genuine
  4822	integral), `E[fg]` as the integral of `f(omega) g(omega)` (equal to the inner
  4823	product by `integral_mul_eq_inner`), `B_r^{1/2}` as `Real.sqrt B`, `r^{-n}` as
  4824	`(r^n)^(-1)` and the tail `sum_{n>N} Z_n` as `tsum_n Z (n + (N+1))`.
  4825	`uniform_series_tail_paper` takes the regularized terms as `Y eps delta n` for
  4826	real `eps, delta`, assumes `r > 1`, `TerminalWickInput` and
  4827	`E|u^{eps,delta}(r)|^2 <= B` for every `eps, delta > 0` (the uniform bound
  4828	`sup_{eps,delta>0} E|u^{eps,delta}(r)|^2 <= B_r`), and `Y^{eps,delta}_n -> X_n` in
  4829	`L^2` for each `n`, where `eps, delta down to 0` is read as the joint limit along
  4830	the product filter `nhdsWithin 0 (Ioi 0) x nhdsWithin 0 (Ioi 0)` (other readings,
  4831	such as iterated limits, are not stated). It proves seven conjuncts: absolute
  4832	convergence of `sum X_n`; `u^{eps,delta}(1) = tsum_n Y^{eps,delta}_n -> u = tsum_n X_n`
  4833	in `L^2` along that filter; the two term bounds and the two tail bounds of
  4834	`E:uniform-series-tail`, the bounds for `Y` for every `eps, delta > 0`; and
  4835	absolute convergence of each `sum_n Y^{eps,delta}_n` ("including absolute
  4836	convergence", line 3662). `uniform_series_tail_second_moment_paper` proves the
  4837	last sentence (lines 3652-3653): if also `E|u^{eps,delta}(1)|^2 <= B_1` for all
  4838	`eps, delta > 0`, then `E|u|^2 <= B_1`. The probability measure
  4839	(`IsProbabilityMeasure mu`) is the manuscript's setting and is carried but not
  4840	used by either wrapper. The general forms `uniform_series_tail` and
  4841	`uniform_series_tail_second_moment` hold in any complete real inner product
  4842	space, for any index type of regularizations and any nontrivial filter, with the
  4843	hypotheses required only eventually along the filter. Proof route: the term
  4844	bound is the TeX's (the double sum `E|u(r)|^2 = sum_{m,n} r^{m+n} E[Y_m Y_n]`
  4845	dominates its diagonal term, `norm_sq_le_of_inner_nonneg`), and the tail bounds
  4846	are the geometric series and the triangle inequality (`tail_bound`). The limit
  4847	`u^{eps,delta}(1) -> u` is proved by Mathlib's dominated convergence for series
  4848	(`tendsto_tsum_of_dominated_convergence`) with the summable majorant
  4849	`B^{1/2} r^{-n}`, instead of the TeX's explicit head/tail split at level `N`
  4850	(lines 3665-3672), which uses the same majorant. No conclusion is narrower than
  4851	the TeX. Junk values are not reached: the scaled series is absolutely summable by

  4802	
  4803	Formalizes `L:uniform-series-tail` (`notes/notes_stratonovich_ham_second_moment.tex`
  4804	at `975feb3`; statement lines 3630-3654 with the display
  4805	`E:uniform-series-tail`, lines 3645-3651; proof lines 3656-3675), with every
  4806	conclusion proved and one supplied input from `L:terminal-wick` (lines
  4807	3527-3572), the structure `TerminalWickInput`. The TeX proof cites exactly two
  4808	facts from `L:terminal-wick` (lines 3657-3658): absolute `L^2` convergence of
  4809	every regularized series and nonnegative mixed moments. `TerminalWickInput mu Y r`
  4810	states these two facts for one family `Y : N -> L^2` and the given `r`:
  4811	`sum_n ||r^n Y_n||_2 < infinity` (`L:terminal-wick` gives it for every real or
  4812	complex `r`, lines 3570-3571) and `E[Y_m Y_n] >= 0` for all `m, n` (its Wick
  4813	formula with nonnegative pairing integrals when the covariance is nonnegative,
  4814	and zero when `m + n` is odd, lines 3566-3568). Nothing else about the Gaussian
  4815	field, the chain measures `g_n^{T,x}` or the Wick formula is used, so the Lean
  4816	statements hold for an arbitrary family of real `L^2(Omega)` elements with these
  4817	two facts; the identification of `Y_n^{eps,delta}` with the terms of
  4818	`L:terminal-wick` for a field with nonnegative covariance is not formalized. The
  4819	fixed point `(T,x)` is implicit in the family. `L^2(Omega)` is Mathlib's
  4820	`Lp R 2 mu` (real-valued), `E|f|^2` is written as the Bochner integral of
  4821	`f(omega)^2` (equal to `||f||^2` by `integral_sq_eq_norm_sq`, a genuine
  4822	integral), `E[fg]` as the integral of `f(omega) g(omega)` (equal to the inner
  4823	product by `integral_mul_eq_inner`), `B_r^{1/2}` as `Real.sqrt B`, `r^{-n}` as
  4824	`(r^n)^(-1)` and the tail `sum_{n>N} Z_n` as `tsum_n Z (n + (N+1))`.
  4825	`uniform_series_tail_paper` takes the regularized terms as `Y eps delta n` for
  4826	real `eps, delta`, assumes `r > 1`, `TerminalWickInput` and
  4827	`E|u^{eps,delta}(r)|^2 <= B` for every `eps, delta > 0` (the uniform bound
  4828	`sup_{eps,delta>0} E|u^{eps,delta}(r)|^2 <= B_r`), and `Y^{eps,delta}_n -> X_n` in
  4829	`L^2` for each `n`, where `eps, delta down to 0` is read as the joint limit along
  4830	the product filter `nhdsWithin 0 (Ioi 0) x nhdsWithin 0 (Ioi 0)` (other readings,
  4831	such as iterated limits, are not stated). It proves seven conjuncts: absolute
  4832	convergence of `sum X_n`; `u^{eps,delta}(1) = tsum_n Y^{eps,delta}_n -> u = tsum_n X_n`
  4833	in `L^2` along that filter; the two term bounds and the two tail bounds of
  4834	`E:uniform-series-tail`, the bounds for `Y` for every `eps, delta > 0`; and
  4835	absolute convergence of each `sum_n Y^{eps,delta}_n` ("including absolute
  4836	convergence", line 3662). `uniform_series_tail_second_moment_paper` proves the
  4837	last sentence (lines 3652-3653): if also `E|u^{eps,delta}(1)|^2 <= B_1` for all
  4838	`eps, delta > 0`, then `E|u|^2 <= B_1`. The probability measure
  4839	(`IsProbabilityMeasure mu`) is the manuscript's setting and is carried but not
  4840	used by either wrapper. The general forms `uniform_series_tail` and
  4841	`uniform_series_tail_second_moment` hold in any complete real inner product
  4842	space, for any index type of regularizations and any nontrivial filter, with the
  4843	hypotheses required only eventually along the filter. Proof route: the term
  4844	bound is the TeX's (the double sum `E|u(r)|^2 = sum_{m,n} r^{m+n} E[Y_m Y_n]`
  4845	dominates its diagonal term, `norm_sq_le_of_inner_nonneg`), and the tail bounds
  4846	are the geometric series and the triangle inequality (`tail_bound`). The limit
  4847	`u^{eps,delta}(1) -> u` is proved by Mathlib's dominated convergence for series
  4848	(`tendsto_tsum_of_dominated_convergence`) with the summable majorant
  4849	`B^{1/2} r^{-n}`, instead of the TeX's explicit head/tail split at level `N`
  4850	(lines 3665-3672), which uses the same majorant. No conclusion is narrower than
  4851	the TeX. Junk values are not reached: the scaled series is absolutely summable by
  4852	hypothesis and the unscaled ones are proved absolutely summable, so every
  4853	`tsum` is a genuine sum; `B >= 0` follows from the moment bound, so
  4854	`Real.sqrt B` is the true square root; `r > 1` makes `(r^n)^(-1)` and
  4855	`1 - r^(-1)` positive. Not formalized: `L:terminal-wick` itself (the Gaussian
  4856	field, the Bochner integrals, `E:terminal-term-majorant`,
  4857	`E:terminal-wick-formula` and the absolute convergence), which is supplied, and
  4858	the application of the lemma to the regularized solution in later proofs.

  4801	## UniformSeriesTail (whole result)
  4802	
  4803	Formalizes `L:uniform-series-tail` (`notes/notes_stratonovich_ham_second_moment.tex`
  4804	at `975feb3`; statement lines 3630-3654 with the display
  4805	`E:uniform-series-tail`, lines 3645-3651; proof lines 3656-3675), with every
  4806	conclusion proved and one supplied input from `L:terminal-wick` (lines
  4807	3527-3572), the structure `TerminalWickInput`. The TeX proof cites exactly two
  4808	facts from `L:terminal-wick` (lines 3657-3658): absolute `L^2` convergence of
  4809	every regularized series and nonnegative mixed moments. `TerminalWickInput mu Y r`
  4810	states these two facts for one family `Y : N -> L^2` and the given `r`:
  4811	`sum_n ||r^n Y_n||_2 < infinity` (`L:terminal-wick` gives it for every real or
  4812	complex `r`, lines 3570-3571) and `E[Y_m Y_n] >= 0` for all `m, n` (its Wick
  4813	formula with nonnegative pairing integrals when the covariance is nonnegative,
  4814	and zero when `m + n` is odd, lines 3566-3568). Nothing else about the Gaussian
  4815	field, the chain measures `g_n^{T,x}` or the Wick formula is used, so the Lean
  4816	statements hold for an arbitrary family of real `L^2(Omega)` elements with these
  4817	two facts; the identification of `Y_n^{eps,delta}` with the terms of
  4818	`L:terminal-wick` for a field with nonnegative covariance is not formalized. The
  4819	fixed point `(T,x)` is implicit in the family. `L^2(Omega)` is Mathlib's
  4820	`Lp R 2 mu` (real-valued), `E|f|^2` is written as the Bochner integral of
  4821	`f(omega)^2` (equal to `||f||^2` by `integral_sq_eq_norm_sq`, a genuine
  4822	integral), `E[fg]` as the integral of `f(omega) g(omega)` (equal to the inner
  4823	product by `integral_mul_eq_inner`), `B_r^{1/2}` as `Real.sqrt B`, `r^{-n}` as
  4824	`(r^n)^(-1)` and the tail `sum_{n>N} Z_n` as `tsum_n Z (n + (N+1))`.
  4825	`uniform_series_tail_paper` takes the regularized terms as `Y eps delta n` for
  4826	real `eps, delta`, assumes `r > 1`, `TerminalWickInput` and
  4827	`E|u^{eps,delta}(r)|^2 <= B` for every `eps, delta > 0` (the uniform bound
  4828	`sup_{eps,delta>0} E|u^{eps,delta}(r)|^2 <= B_r`), and `Y^{eps,delta}_n -> X_n` in
  4829	`L^2` for each `n`, where `eps, delta down to 0` is read as the joint limit along
  4830	the product filter `nhdsWithin 0 (Ioi 0) x nhdsWithin 0 (Ioi 0)` (other readings,
  4831	such as iterated limits, are not stated). It proves seven conjuncts: absolute
  4832	convergence of `sum X_n`; `u^{eps,delta}(1) = tsum_n Y^{eps,delta}_n -> u = tsum_n X_n`
  4833	in `L^2` along that filter; the two term bounds and the two tail bounds of
  4834	`E:uniform-series-tail`, the bounds for `Y` for every `eps, delta > 0`; and
  4835	absolute convergence of each `sum_n Y^{eps,delta}_n` ("including absolute
  4836	convergence", line 3662). `uniform_series_tail_second_moment_paper` proves the
  4837	last sentence (lines 3652-3653): if also `E|u^{eps,delta}(1)|^2 <= B_1` for all
  4838	`eps, delta > 0`, then `E|u|^2 <= B_1`. The probability measure
  4839	(`IsProbabilityMeasure mu`) is the manuscript's setting and is carried but not
  4840	used by either wrapper. The general forms `uniform_series_tail` and
  4841	`uniform_series_tail_second_moment` hold in any complete real inner product
  4842	space, for any index type of regularizations and any nontrivial filter, with the
  4843	hypotheses required only eventually along the filter. Proof route: the term
  4844	bound is the TeX's (the double sum `E|u(r)|^2 = sum_{m,n} r^{m+n} E[Y_m Y_n]`
  4845	dominates its diagonal term, `norm_sq_le_of_inner_nonneg`), and the tail bounds
  4846	are the geometric series and the triangle inequality (`tail_bound`). The limit
  4847	`u^{eps,delta}(1) -> u` is proved by Mathlib's dominated convergence for series
  4848	(`tendsto_tsum_of_dominated_convergence`) with the summable majorant
  4849	`B^{1/2} r^{-n}`, instead of the TeX's explicit head/tail split at level `N`
  4850	(lines 3665-3672), which uses the same majorant. No conclusion is narrower than
  4851	the TeX. Junk values are not reached: the scaled series is absolutely summable by
  4852	hypothesis and the unscaled ones are proved absolutely summable, so every
  4853	`tsum` is a genuine sum; `B >= 0` follows from the moment bound, so
  4854	`Real.sqrt B` is the true square root; `r > 1` makes `(r^n)^(-1)` and
  4855	`1 - r^(-1)` positive. Not formalized: `L:terminal-wick` itself (the Gaussian
  4856	field, the Bochner integrals, `E:terminal-term-majorant`,
  4857	`E:terminal-wick-formula` and the absolute convergence), which is supplied, and
  4858	the application of the lemma to the regularized solution in later proofs.

     1	\section{Physical spatial pairings and the full occupation class}
     2	\label{S:spatial-occupation-foundation}
     3	
     4	Retain a nonzero original covariance from Hypothesis~\ref{H:homog} with its
     5	amplitude. Set $a = \alpha_0$, $k = 3-\alpha > 1$, $q = 4-\alpha = k+1$ and $D =
     6	q-2a > 0$. The scalar $D$ is fixed. All profiles are real. The original positive
     7	temporal exponent and threshold imply $\alpha < 2$; this is the strict
     8	inequality used in the scalar powers and concavity. The finite variational value
     9	over nonnegative controls $S_1^{\mathrm{pos}}$ is that of
    10	Proposition~\ref{P:variational-positive-scores}.
    11	
    12	\begin{lemma}[The physical two-point integral]\label{L:spatial-physical-pair}
    13	  The positive measure $\nu(\ud x,\ud y) = \ud x\,\Gamma(\ud y)$ is
    14	  sigma-finite. For nonnegative functions define
    15	  \begin{equation}\label{E:spatial-physical-pair}
    16	    B_\Gamma(f,h)=\int f(x)h(x-y)\nu(\ud x,\ud y)
    17	  \end{equation}
    18	  initially as an extended nonnegative integral, using finite Borel
    19	  representatives of Lebesgue classes. Its value is representative independent.
    20	  Lebesgue-a.e. convergence transfers to $\nu$-a.e. convergence at both
    21	  positions $x$ and $x-y$.
    22	\end{lemma}
    23	
    24	\begin{proof}
    25	  Local finiteness of $\Gamma$ gives sigma-finiteness on exhausting balls, and
    26	  Lebesgue measure is sigma-finite. If $N$ is Borel and Lebesgue null, Tonelli
    27	  applied first in $x$ gives $\nu\{x\in N\} = 0$ and $\nu\{x-y\in N\} = 0$,
    28	  because every fixed translate of $N$ is null. An arbitrary Lebesgue null set
    29	  has a Borel null superset. Thus, arbitrary versions are measurable in the
    30	  $\nu$ completion with the same value, and the same observation applies to the
    31	  exceptional sets of a.e. convergence. Signed pairings will be used only after
    32	  absolute convergence. This proves Lemma~\ref{L:spatial-physical-pair}.
    33	\end{proof}

    48	  positive $c$ interval. With the exact $M_a$
    49	  in~\eqref{E:temporal-equilibrium-mass},

    56	\begin{proof}

    58	  $k_f(s_0) = \int_0^1|s_0-t|^{-a}f(t)\ud t > 0$. The smooth test $\Psi(t,x) =
    59	  cf(t)z(x)/k_f(s_0)$ has mean $cU_z$ at $s_0$.
    60	  Proposition~\ref{P:variational-unmasked-rate} gives boundedness of this
    61	  potential, the displayed real Rayleigh formula, and a positive rate for every
    62	  $c > 0$. Comparing identical unit tests makes $\lambda_z(c)^2$ Lipschitz with
    63	  constant $\|U_z\|_\infty$. On a positive compact interval its rate has a
    64	  positive floor by monotonicity, giving the square-root Lipschitz bound.

    66	  Use the nonincreasing smooth cutoff $\chi$ constructed in the proof of
    67	  Proposition~\ref{P:variational-remove-mask}. For integers $n \ge 4$, set on
    68	  $(0,1)$
    69	  \[
    70	    f_n(t)=f_a(t)\chi(1/(nt))\chi(1/(n(1-t))),\qquad
    71	    k_n(s)=\int_0^1|s-t|^{-a}f_n(t)\ud t.
    72	  \]

    74	  nonzero, and increases to $f_a$. Thus, $\Psi_n = f_n\otimes z$ is a positive
    75	  smooth control. Monotone convergence
    76	  and~\eqref{E:temporal-equilibrium-potential} give $k_n(s)\uparrow1$ for every
    77	  $s \in [0,1]$. Since the kernel is at least one on the unit square off its
    78	  null diagonal, $0 < c_0: = \int_0^1f_4 \le k_n(s) \le 1$. The mean is
    79	  $k_n(s)U_z$; hence its rate is $\lambda_z(k_n(s))$, converging to
    80	  $\lambda_z(1)$ and bounded by that finite number. Dominated convergence gives
    81	  $I_{\Psi_n} \to \lambda_z(1)$.

    83	  The Gaussian cost is exactly the nonnegative Tonelli pairing
    84	  \[
    85	    v_{\Psi_n}=B_\Gamma(z,z)\int_0^1f_n(s)k_n(s)\ud s.

    88	  $M_aB_\Gamma(z,z)$. The spatial factor is finite and positive: its smooth
    89	  compact autocorrelation is positive near zero, and homogeneity scales any
    90	  origin-centered ball of positive $\Gamma$ mass to every other positive radius.

    92	  inequalities $S_1^{\mathrm{pos}} \ge I_{\Psi_n}-v_{\Psi_n}/2$. The variational
    93	  expression differences need not increase. No control depends on original large
    94	  time and no rough stochastic evolution has been used. This proves

   117	  densely defined, symmetric and closed on $H^2$; the two graph norms are
   118	  equivalent under a bounded perturbation. For real $b > M$,
   119	  \[
   120	    H_s-ib=(I+B_s(A-ib)^{-1})(A-ib).
   121	  \]
   122	  The first factor has a Neumann inverse because $\|B_s(A-ib)^{-1}\| \le M/b <
   123	  1$, and the same holds with $+ib$. To check self-adjointness directly, for $u
   124	  \in D(H_s^*)$ solve $(H_s-ib)v = (H_s^*-ib)u$ with $v \in D(H_s)$. Then $u-v
   125	  \in \ker(H_s^*-ib) = \operatorname{Ran}(H_s+ib)^\perp = \{0\}$. Hence,
   126	  $D(H_s^*) = D(H_s)$.
   127	
   128	  Set $c_{\mathrm{shift}} = 1+M$ and $J_s = H_s+c_{\mathrm{shift}} \ge 1$.
   129	  Integration by parts on $H^2$ gives
   130	  \[
   131	    \|J_s^{1/2}f\|_2^2=q_s(f)+c_{\mathrm{shift}}\|f\|_2^2,\qquad
   132	    \|f\|_{H^1}^2\le\|J_s^{1/2}f\|_2^2
   133	    \le c_{\mathrm{shift}}\|f\|_{H^1}^2.
   134	  \]
   135	  Spectral cutoffs $1_{[1,n]}(J_s)$ show that $H^2 = D(J_s)$ is a core for the
   136	  half-power norm; Fourier cutoffs give its density in $H^1$. Completion in the
   137	  equivalent norms identifies $D(J_s^{1/2})$ and $H^1$ as $L^2$ subspaces, since
   138	  both norms dominate $L^2$. This proves the stated form domain.
   139	
   140	  The spectral lower bound gives one direction of the Rayleigh identity. For the
   141	  reverse, nonzero spectral projections in $[E_s,E_s+\epsilon]$ give unit $H^2$
   142	  vectors with Rayleigh values at most $E_s+\epsilon$. The bottom is finite
   143	  because the operator is bounded below and has finite Rayleigh tests. Let
   144	  $\epsilon\downarrow0$. Real tests give the same infimum: $q_s(u+iv) =
   145	  q_s(u)+q_s(v)$, so the quotient is the norm-weighted average of the nonzero
   146	  real quotients. This proves the Rayleigh identity with $-E_s$ on the left. The
   147	  following negative upper bound justifies writing that value as
   148	  $\lambda_{\Psi,s}^2$ in~\eqref{E:variational-real-rayleigh}.
   149	
   150	  Proposition~\ref{P:compact-original-common-trial} supplies, for this original
   151	  $\Psi$, one unit compactly supported $w$ and a finite plateau mask with a
   152	  common strictly negative upper bound $\epsilon_0 > 0$. Its trial has support
   153	  in $B_{2L}$; choose its plateau radius $R_0 \ge 2L$. The unmasked form on this
   154	  same $w$ is no larger. Consequently, $-M \le E_s \le -\epsilon_0 < 0$, and
   155	  $\sqrt{\epsilon_0} \le \lambda_{\Psi,s} \le \sqrt M$. Comparing identical unit
   156	  form tests gives $|E_s-E_t| \le \|h_s-h_t\|_\infty$ and therefore
   157	  \[
   158	    |\lambda_{\Psi,s}-\lambda_{\Psi,t}|
   159	    \le \frac{C_\Psi}{2\sqrt{\epsilon_0}}|s-t|.
   160	  \]
   161	  This also proves positivity and finiteness of $I_\Psi$. No compact-potential
   162	  spectral theorem was applied to $H_s$. This proves
   163	  Proposition~\ref{P:variational-unmasked-rate}.
   164	\end{proof}

   316	\begin{proposition}[The full physical occupation class]
   317	  \label{P:occupation-physical-class}
   318	  The pairings $(s,t)\mapsto B_\Gamma(g_s^2,g_t^2)$ are measurable,
   319	  representative independent and equal to their physical integrals. With
   320	  \[
   321	    J(g)=\int_0^1\int_0^1

   323	  \]

   325	  \begin{equation}\label{E:occupation-physical-bound}
   326	    0\le J(g)\le R_\star R_{\mathrm{sp}}T(g)^{\alpha/2}<\infty.
   327	  \end{equation}

   329	  \begin{equation}\label{E:occupation-own-energy}
   330	    0<\mathcal{E}_\star^{\mathcal{O}}
   331	    :=\sup_{g\in\mathcal{O}}\big(J(g)-T(g)/2\big)

   339	  strong representative and replace exceptional null times by one fixed real
   340	  unit compact bump. Joint measurable spatial representatives exist: approximate
   341	  this Bochner $L^2$ field by simple $H^1$-valued functions with summable
   342	  $L^2(0,1;H^1)$ errors, and choose measurable spatial versions for their
   343	  countably many values. A subsequence has a measurable spacetime $L^2$ limit,
   344	  and for a.e. $s$ its spatial $L^2$ class is $g_s$.

   346	  spatial versions. The continuous pairing map on the separable space $H^1\times
   347	  H^1$ from Proposition~\ref{P:spatial-four-linear} consequently gives a
   348	  measurable function of $(s,t)$ agreeing a.e. with the nonnegative physical

   351	  Set $F(s) = b(g_s)^{\alpha/4}$. Equations~\eqref{E:spatial-homogeneous-bound}

  3016	      (1+k_i/(\lambda h_i))^{\ell_i}.
  3017	    \end{split}
  3018	  \end{equation}
  3019	  In particular, a singleton used twice on one copy has $\ell_i = 1$; a higher
  3020	  color has at most two metric factors.
  3021	\end{lemma}

3329	\begin{proposition}[Uniform interval coefficients]\label{P:interval-coefficients}
  3330	  There is $C = C(\alpha,\alpha_0,L,c)$ such that, for real Schwartz phase $v$,
  3331	  every $k \ge 1$ satisfies
  3332	  \begin{equation}\label{E:interval-coefficient-bound}
  3333	    \left|[s^{2k}]\E\|\mathcal{U}_{\mathcal{F}}^\epsilon(T;s)v\|_{1/T}^2\right|
  3334	    \le\frac{C^k R_\alpha^k T^{\beta k}}{(k!)^\nu}\|v\|_{1/T}^2,
  3335	  \end{equation}
  3336	  uniformly in $\epsilon > 0$ and the finite family. In particular,
  3337	  \begin{equation}\label{E:interval-phase-bound}
  3338	    \E\|\mathcal{U}_{\mathcal{F}}^\epsilon(T;1)v\|_{1/T}^2
  3339	    \le e\exp\{C R_\alpha^{1/\nu}T^{\beta/\nu}\}\|v\|_{1/T}^2.
  3340	  \end{equation}
  3341	\end{proposition}
  3342	
  3343	\begin{proof}
  3344	  Zero noise is trivial; omit any zero $\sigma_i$. Enlarge the interval-length
  3345	  constant $L$ to $\max\{1,L\}$ if necessary. The hypotheses remain true and the
  3346	  final constant may depend on $L$, so throughout this proof we may assume $L
  3347	  \ge 1$. Replacing $(\sigma_i,W_i^\epsilon)$ by
  3348	  $(|\sigma_i|,\operatorname{sgn}(\sigma_i)W_i^\epsilon)$ leaves the potential
  3349	  unchanged and preserves the joint law of the independent real Gaussian fields.
  3350	  Thus, we may assume $\sigma_i > 0$. We first work with finitely many Gaussian
  3351	  coordinates of each field and a bounded spatial Fourier band. Denote their
  3352	  common phase Hilbert space by $\mathcal{H}_\rho = L^2(\Omega;X_\rho)$. The
  3353	  initial data are projected to the band. This contracts every $X_\rho$ norm; we
  3354	  keep the original $\|v\|_\rho$ on the right of the estimates. The projections
  3355	  converge strongly to the original data.
  3356	
  3357	  \emph{Ordinary coefficients and their existence.} Fix $\lambda > 0$
  3358	  temporarily. Give interval $i$ its own amplitude $z_i$ and write
  3359	  \[
  3360	    \mathcal{U}(T;\boldsymbol z)v
  3361	    =\sum_{\boldsymbol r\in\N_0^{\mathcal{F}}}
  3362	    \boldsymbol z^{\boldsymbol r}U_{\boldsymbol r}v.
  3363	  \]
  3364	  These are ordinary power-series coefficients, without factorials incorporated
  3365	  in their definition. At fixed smoothing and finite interval family, put
  3366	  $v_{\max} = \sup_t\sum_i\sigma_i^2\mathbf1_{I_i}(t) \Gamma_\epsilon(0) <
  3367	  \infty$. On Gaussian degrees at most $n$, multiplication by the instantaneous
  3368	  field has norm at most $2\sqrt{n+1}\sqrt{v_{\max}}$. The free phase has norm
  3369	  at most $e^{\lambda h/2}$ in $X_\lambda$, and a phase insertion
  3370	  $(u,w)\mapsto(0,Wu)$ costs at most its unweighted multiplication norm divided
  3371	  by $\lambda$. Thus, on $\max_i|z_i| \le z_*$ the total order-$n$ phase is
  3372	  bounded by
  3373	  \begin{equation}\label{E:interval-entire-majorant}
  3374	    e^{\lambda T/2}
  3375	    \frac{(2z_*\sqrt{n+1}\sqrt{v_{\max}}T/\lambda)^n}{n!}
  3376	    \|v\|_\lambda .
  3377	  \end{equation}
  3378	  The series of these bounds converges for every finite $z_*$. Its locally
  3379	  uniform convergence defines an entire vector function. We also verify
  3380	  coefficientwise absolute convergence. Fix $z_* > 0$ and put
  3381	  \[
  3382	    K_{2z_*}=\sup_{\max_i|z_i|\le2z_*}
  3383	    \|\mathcal{U}(T;\boldsymbol z)v\|_{\mathcal{H}_{1/T}}<\infty,
  3384	  \]
  3385	  using the majorant with its temporary parameter $\lambda = 1/T$. Normalized
  3386	  vector Cauchy integration on this larger polydisc gives
  3387	  \[
  3388	    \|U_{\boldsymbol r}v\|_{\mathcal{H}_{1/T}}
  3389	    \le K_{2z_*}(2z_*)^{-|\boldsymbol r|},\qquad
  3390	    \sum_{\boldsymbol r}z_*^{|\boldsymbol r|}
  3391	    \|U_{\boldsymbol r}v\|_{\mathcal{H}_{1/T}}
  3392	    \le2^{|\mathcal{F}|}K_{2z_*}.
  3393	  \]
  3394	  The sum is the product of $|\mathcal{F}|$ geometric series. Cauchy--Schwarz
  3395	  therefore bounds the absolute energy double series by
  3396	  $4^{|\mathcal{F}|}K_{2z_*}^2$. This finite factor justifies the coefficient
  3397	  identities at fixed family and smoothing; it does not enter the uniform
  3398	  coefficient estimate below.
  3399	
  3400	  Set $Q_{\boldsymbol r,\boldsymbol q} = \langle U_{\boldsymbol
  3401	  r}v,U_{\boldsymbol q}v \rangle_{\mathcal{H}_{1/T}}$. Both vectors use the same
  3402	  Gaussian fields. Independence is between distinct colors, not between the two
  3403	  copies in this inner product. For real $s$, substitution $z_i = s$ gives the
  3404	  exact identity
  3405	  \begin{equation}\label{E:interval-energy-splits}
  3406	    [s^{2k}]\E\|\mathcal{U}(T;s)v\|_{1/T}^2
  3407	    =\sum_{|\boldsymbol r|+|\boldsymbol q|=2k}
  3408	    Q_{\boldsymbol r,\boldsymbol q}.
  3409	  \end{equation}
  3410	  Reflection of Gaussian color $i$ multiplies $U_{\boldsymbol r}v$ by
  3411	  $(-1)^{r_i}$. Hence, $Q_{\boldsymbol r,\boldsymbol q} = 0$ unless $r_i+q_i =
  3412	  2k_i$ for every $i$, where $\sum_i k_i = k$. If $k_i = 0$, both coefficients
  3413	  are obtained by setting $z_i = 0$; this removes that field exactly. There are
  3414	  at most $k$ active colors. For fixed $\boldsymbol k$, the number of splits is
  3415	  $\prod_i(2k_i+1) \le 3^k$.
  3416	
  3417	  For this fixed $\boldsymbol k$, truncate the Hermite degree of color $i$ at
  3418	  $N_i = 2k_i$. A word contributing to $U_{\boldsymbol r}$ has $r_i \le 2k_i$
  3419	  insertions of color $i$, and the other copy has $q_i \le 2k_i$.
  3420	  Lemma~\ref{L:finite-word-cutoff}, with the spatial phase space as
  3421	  $\mathscr{X}$ and free phase factors between insertions, therefore preserves
  3422	  both selected vector coefficients exactly. Their Duhamel time integrals and
  3423	  finite word sums preserve the equality. Creation followed by annihilation is
  3424	  retained; there is no Hermite-degree limit in this coefficient calculation.
  3476	  \emph{Identification and summation.} Keep positive smoothing, finite interval
  3477	  family and a fixed coefficient. The finite-degree multiplication bound used
  3478	  in~\eqref{E:interval-entire-majorant} is uniform in mode and band cutoffs. On
  3479	  finite-coordinate Gaussian vectors the omitted annihilation tail is zero and
  3480	  the creation tail tends to zero by its omitted pointwise variances and
  3481	  dominated convergence. Density in each finite degree extends this strong
  3482	  convergence. Closedness identifies the limit with multiplication by the
  3483	  measurable smoothed field. Fourier projections converge strongly and commute
  3484	  with free evolution. Dominated time integration thus identifies every fixed
  3485	  Duhamel word. The selected coefficients of the local Hermite truncation were
  3486	  already equal to those untruncated words. The full series is constructed
  3487	  separately using~\eqref{E:interval-entire-majorant}, choosing a sufficient
  3488	  degree cutoff anew at each order. A fixed-degree truncated propagator is not
  3489	  identified with the full evolution. The entire majorant gives convergence
  3490	  uniformly on compact amplitude sets. The coefficients estimated above are
  3491	  therefore those of the finite-interval model, with no zero-smoothing limit at
  3492	  this step.
  3493	
  3494	  The nonuniform number $v_{\max}$ was used only for this identification. The
  3495	  uniform coefficient bound contains no such number. Its constants come from
  3496	  $\delta_{\alpha/2}$, the fixed phase bound, the interval-length bound lemma
  3497	  and $L,c$; covariance enters only through $R_\alpha^k$. The zero-order energy
  3498	  is at most $e\|v\|_{1/T}^2$. Put $x = CR_\alpha T^\beta$ and $Y = e^{\nu
  3499	  x^{1/\nu}} \ge 1$. Since $\nu > 1$, $\sum_{k\ge0}x^k/(k!)^\nu \le Y$. Summing
  3500	  the coefficient bounds in absolute value gives
  3501	  \[
  3502	    \E\|\mathcal{U}(T;1)v\|_{1/T}^2
  3503	    \le(e+Y-1)\|v\|_{1/T}^2\le eY\|v\|_{1/T}^2.
  3504	  \]
  3505	  Absorbing $\nu C^{1/\nu}$ into the parameter-only constant proves
  3506	  \eqref{E:interval-phase-bound}. This proves
  3507	  Proposition~\ref{P:interval-coefficients}.
  3508	\end{proof}
